svg.title: The Design of Everyday Things — reconstructed back cover
svg.desc: Editable recreation from a user-supplied reference. Text, panels and ISBN barcode are vector elements.
svg.text: BUSINESS / PSYCHOLOGY
“Part operating manual for designers and part manifesto on the power of designing for people.

text.tspan: is even more relevant today than it was when first published.”
—TIM BROWN, CEO, IDEO, and author of

svg.text: E

text.tspan: ven the smartest among us can feel inept as we try to figure out the shower control in a hotel or
attempt to navigate an unfamiliar television set or stove. When
was published in 1988, Don Norman proposed that the fault lies not in ourselves but in product de-
sign that ignores the needs of users and the principles of cognitive psychology. Alas, bad design
is everywhere, but fortunately, it isn’t difficult to design things that are understandable, usable, and
enjoyable. Thoughtfully revised to keep the timeless principles of psychology up to date with ever-
is a powerful appeal for good design, and
a reminder of how—and why—some products satisfy customers while others only frustrate them.

svg.text: “Design may be our top competitive edge. This book is a joy—fun and of the utmost importance.”
“This book changed the field of design. As the pace of technological change accelerates, the
principles in this book are increasingly important. The new examples and ideas
about design and about everyday life and leadership are extraordinary.”
—PATRICK WHITNEY, Dean, Institute of Design, Steelcase/Robert C. Pew
Professor of Design, Illinois Institute of Technology
“Norman enlightens us on the psychology of people and things and how they interact. He
continues to inspire me as a professor of design. The cumulated insights in this book and the cross-
disciplinary nature of design make The Design of Everyday Things a special treasure and a joy for
designers who are interested in advancing their discipline.”
—CEES DE BONT, Dean, School of Design and Chair Professor of
Industrial Design, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University
DON NORMAN
is a co-founder of the Nielsen Norman Group, and holds graduate degrees

text.tspan: in engineering and psychology. His many books include
. He lives in Silicon Valley, California.
